description: Comprehensive Geometry question bank derived from SSLC-level Geometry notes (Chapter 8.3). Covers all topics: foundations, angles, triangles, quadrilaterals, circles, polygons, symmetry, and coordinate geometry. Designed for KEA examination preparation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the branch of mathematics concerned with shapes, sizes, positions, distances and properties of figures?
questions.explanation: Geometry is the branch of mathematics concerned with shapes, sizes, positions, distances and properties of figures in a plane or in space.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is an exact position with no length, breadth or thickness called?
questions.explanation: A point is an exact position with no length, breadth or thickness; it is represented by a dot and a capital letter.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A straight path extending endlessly in both directions is called a:
questions.explanation: A line is a straight path extending endlessly in both directions; it has length but no thickness.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is a part of a line bounded by two endpoints called?
questions.explanation: A line segment is a part of a line bounded by two endpoints; it has a definite length.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A part of a line with one endpoint that extends endlessly in one direction is called a:
questions.explanation: A ray is a part of a line with one endpoint that extends endlessly in one direction.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is a flat two-dimensional surface that extends without end in all directions called?
questions.explanation: A plane is a flat two-dimensional surface that extends without end in all directions.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Points that lie on the same straight line are called:
questions.explanation: Collinear points are points that lie on the same straight line.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Points that lie in the same plane are called:
questions.explanation: Coplanar points are points that lie in the same plane.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Two lines that meet at a point are called:
questions.explanation: Intersecting lines are two lines that meet at a point.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Coplanar straight lines that never meet, however far they are extended, are called:
questions.explanation: Parallel lines are coplanar straight lines that never meet; the perpendicular distance between them remains constant.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Lines that intersect to form a right angle of 90° are called:
questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines are lines that intersect to form a right angle of 90°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Three or more lines that pass through one common point are called:
questions.explanation: Concurrent lines are three or more lines that pass through one common point.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A line that intersects two or more other lines at distinct points is called a:
questions.explanation: A transversal is a line that intersects two or more other lines at distinct points.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The distance between two points on a line is:

options.A: The length of the line segment joining them
options.B: The perpendicular distance from a third point

questions.explanation: The distance between two points on a line is the length of the line segment joining them.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The point that divides a line segment into two equal segments is called the:
questions.explanation: The midpoint of a line segment is the point that divides the segment into two equal segments.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A line, ray or segment that divides an angle or segment into two equal parts is called a:
questions.explanation: A bisector is a line, ray or segment that divides an angle or segment into two equal parts.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A line perpendicular to a segment at its midpoint is called the:
questions.explanation: The perpendicular bisector of a segment is a line perpendicular to a segment at its midpoint; every point on it is equidistant from the segment's endpoints.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The shortest distance from a point to a line is:

options.A: Any line segment from the point to the line
options.B: The length of the perpendicular segment from the point to the line
options.C: The length of the longest segment from the point to the line

questions.explanation: The shortest distance from a point to a line is the length of the perpendicular segment from the point to the line.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: How many lines can pass through two distinct points?
questions.explanation: Exactly one straight line can pass through two distinct points.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: How many lines can pass through one point?
questions.explanation: Infinitely many lines can pass through one point.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A figure formed by two rays having a common endpoint is called a(n):
questions.explanation: An angle is a figure formed by two rays having a common endpoint called the vertex.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The common endpoint of the two rays forming an angle is called the:
questions.explanation: The vertex of an angle is the common endpoint of the two rays forming the angle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The two rays that form an angle are called its:
questions.explanation: The arms of an angle are the two rays that form the angle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: In what unit are angles commonly measured in school geometry?
questions.explanation: Angles are commonly measured in degrees (°); a full turn is 360°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A full turn is equal to how many degrees?
questions.explanation: A full turn is 360°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: An angle measuring 0° is called a:
questions.explanation: A zero angle is an angle measuring 0°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: An angle greater than 0° but less than 90° is called a(n):
questions.explanation: An acute angle is greater than 0° but less than 90°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: An angle measuring exactly 90° is called a:
questions.explanation: A right angle is an angle measuring exactly 90°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: An angle greater than 90° but less than 180° is called a(n):
questions.explanation: An obtuse angle is greater than 90° but less than 180°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: An angle measuring exactly 180° is called a:
questions.explanation: A straight angle is an angle measuring exactly 180°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: An angle greater than 180° but less than 360° is called a:
questions.explanation: A reflex angle is greater than 180° but less than 360°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: An angle measuring 360° is called a:
questions.explanation: A complete angle is an angle measuring 360°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Two angles whose sum is 90° are called:
questions.explanation: Complementary angles are two angles whose sum is 90°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Two angles whose sum is 180° are called:
questions.explanation: Supplementary angles are two angles whose sum is 180°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Two angles sharing a common vertex and a common arm, with non-overlapping interiors, are called:
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles are two angles sharing a common vertex and a common arm, with non-overlapping interiors.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A pair of adjacent angles whose non-common arms form a straight line is called a:
questions.explanation: A linear pair is a pair of adjacent angles whose non-common arms form a straight line; their sum is 180°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The sum of angles in a linear pair is:
questions.explanation: A linear pair consists of adjacent angles whose non-common arms form a straight line; their sum is 180°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The opposite angles formed when two straight lines intersect are called:
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are the opposite angles formed when two straight lines intersect; each pair is equal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If one angle in a linear pair is 65°, what is the other angle?
questions.explanation: The other angle is 115°, because 180° - 65° = 115°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If one of two vertically opposite angles is 72°, what is the opposite angle?
questions.explanation: The opposite angle is 72°, because vertically opposite angles are equal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the angle sum around a point?
questions.explanation: The angle sum around a point is 360°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the sum of angles on a straight line?
questions.explanation: The sum of angles on a straight line is 180°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: When a ray stands on a straight line, the two adjacent angles formed make a:
questions.explanation: When a ray stands on a straight line, the two adjacent angles formed make a linear pair and sum to 180°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: When a transversal cuts parallel lines, angles in matching relative positions at the two intersections are called:
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are angles in matching relative positions at the two intersections; corresponding angles are equal when lines are parallel.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Angles between two lines and on opposite sides of a transversal are called:
questions.explanation: Alternate interior angles are angles between the two lines and on opposite sides of a transversal; they are equal when the lines are parallel.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Angles outside two lines and on opposite sides of a transversal are called:
questions.explanation: Alternate exterior angles are angles outside the two lines and on opposite sides of a transversal; they are equal when the lines are parallel.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Interior angles on the same side of a transversal are called:
questions.explanation: Co-interior (same-side interior) angles are interior angles on the same side of a transversal; when the lines are parallel, they sum to 180°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If a transversal cuts parallel lines and one corresponding angle is 110°, what is the matching corresponding angle?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal when lines are parallel, so the matching angle is 110°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If parallel lines are cut by a transversal and one co-interior angle is 70°, what is the other?
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles are supplementary when lines are parallel, so the other angle is 180° - 70° = 110°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A ray from the vertex that divides an angle into two equal angles is called the:
questions.explanation: The angle bisector of an angle is a ray from the vertex that divides the angle into two equal angles.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the angle sum of a triangle?
questions.explanation: The angle sum of a triangle is 180°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the angle sum of a quadrilateral?
questions.explanation: The angle sum of a quadrilateral is 360°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A polygon with three sides, three vertices and three interior angles is called a:
questions.explanation: A triangle is a polygon with three sides, three vertices and three interior angles.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the sum of the interior angles of every triangle?
questions.explanation: The sum of the interior angles of every triangle is 180°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: An angle formed by one side of a triangle and the extension of an adjacent side is called a(n):
questions.explanation: An exterior angle of a triangle is an angle formed by one side and the extension of an adjacent side.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: According to the exterior-angle property of a triangle, an exterior angle equals:

options.B: The sum of the two opposite (remote) interior angles
options.C: The difference of the two opposite interior angles

questions.explanation: An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two opposite (remote) interior angles.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The triangle inequality theorem states that:

options.A: The sum of any two sides is equal to the third side
options.B: The sum of the lengths of any two sides must be greater than the length of the third side
options.C: The sum of the lengths of any two sides must be less than the third side
options.D: All three sides must be equal

questions.explanation: The triangle inequality theorem states that the sum of the lengths of any two sides of a triangle must be greater than the length of the third side.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: In a triangle, the longer side is opposite the:
questions.explanation: The longer side is opposite the larger angle; equal sides are opposite equal angles.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A triangle with all three sides equal is called a(n):
questions.explanation: An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal; each interior angle is 60°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Each interior angle of an equilateral triangle measures:
questions.explanation: Each interior angle of an equilateral triangle is 60°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A triangle with at least two equal sides is called a(n):
questions.explanation: An isosceles triangle has at least two equal sides; the angles opposite those equal sides are equal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: In an isosceles triangle, the angles opposite the equal sides are:
questions.explanation: In an isosceles triangle, the angles opposite the equal sides are equal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A triangle with all three sides of different lengths is called a(n):
questions.explanation: A scalene triangle has all three sides of different lengths; all three angles are different.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A triangle in which all three angles are less than 90° is called a(n):
questions.explanation: An acute-angled triangle is a triangle in which all three angles are less than 90°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A triangle with one angle equal to 90° is called a(n):
questions.explanation: A right-angled triangle is a triangle with one angle equal to 90°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A triangle with one angle greater than 90° is called a(n):
questions.explanation: An obtuse-angled triangle is a triangle with one angle greater than 90°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Can a triangle have two right angles?

options.B: No, because the sum of its interior angles would exceed 180°

questions.explanation: A triangle cannot have two right angles because the sum of its interior angles would exceed 180°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Can a triangle have two obtuse angles?

options.B: No, because the sum of its interior angles would exceed 180°

questions.explanation: A triangle cannot have two obtuse angles because the sum of its interior angles would exceed 180°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The side opposite the right angle in a right-angled triangle is called the:
questions.explanation: The hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle in a right-angled triangle; it is the longest side.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The Pythagorean theorem states that in a right-angled triangle:

options.A: The square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides
options.B: The hypotenuse equals the sum of the other two sides
options.C: The square of the hypotenuse equals the difference of the squares of the other two sides

questions.explanation: The Pythagorean theorem states that c² = a² + b², where c is the hypotenuse.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A right triangle has perpendicular sides 3 cm and 4 cm. What is its hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: The hypotenuse is 5 cm, because √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The converse of the Pythagorean theorem states that:

options.A: If a triangle is right-angled, then c² = a² + b²
options.B: If the square of the longest side equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides, the triangle is right-angled
options.D: The hypotenuse is always the shortest side

questions.explanation: The converse states that if the square of the longest side of a triangle equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides, the triangle is right-angled.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The perimeter of a triangle is:

options.A: Half the product of base and height
options.B: The sum of its three side lengths
options.C: The product of its three sides

questions.explanation: The perimeter of a triangle is the sum of its three side lengths: Perimeter = a + b + c.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The area of a triangle is:

options.B: Half the product of its base and the perpendicular height to that base

questions.explanation: The area of a triangle is half the product of its base and the perpendicular height to that base.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The area of a right-angled triangle is:

options.A: Half the product of its two perpendicular sides
options.B: The product of the hypotenuse and base
options.C: The sum of its three sides

questions.explanation: The area of a right-angled triangle is half the product of its two perpendicular sides.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Heron's formula for the area of a triangle with sides a, b, c is:
questions.explanation: Heron's formula: Area = √[s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)], where s = (a+b+c)/2 is the semiperimeter.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: In Heron's formula, s represents the:
questions.explanation: In Heron's formula, s = (a+b+c)/2 is the semiperimeter, which is half the perimeter.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The semiperimeter of a triangle is:
questions.explanation: The semiperimeter of a triangle is half its perimeter.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A segment joining a vertex of a triangle to the midpoint of the opposite side is called a:
questions.explanation: The median of a triangle is a segment joining a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A perpendicular segment from a vertex of a triangle to the line containing the opposite side is called a(n):
questions.explanation: The altitude of a triangle is a perpendicular segment from a vertex to the line containing the opposite side.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A segment or ray from a vertex of a triangle that divides that angle into two equal angles is called a(n):
questions.explanation: An angle bisector in a triangle is a segment or ray from a vertex that divides that angle into two equal angles.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A line perpendicular to a side of a triangle at its midpoint is called a:
questions.explanation: A perpendicular bisector in a triangle is a line perpendicular to a side at its midpoint.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The point where the three medians of a triangle meet is called the:
questions.explanation: The centroid is the point where the three medians meet; it divides each median in the ratio 2:1 measured from the vertex.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The centroid divides each median in what ratio measured from the vertex?
questions.explanation: The centroid divides each median in the ratio 2:1 measured from the vertex.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The point where the three internal angle bisectors of a triangle meet is called the:
questions.explanation: The incenter is the point where the three internal angle bisectors meet; it is the centre of the incircle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The point where the perpendicular bisectors of the three sides of a triangle meet is called the:
questions.explanation: The circumcenter is the point where the perpendicular bisectors of the three sides meet; it is the centre of the circumcircle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The point where the three altitudes of a triangle, or their extensions, meet is called the:
questions.explanation: The orthocenter is the point where the three altitudes, or their extensions, meet.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Where is the circumcenter of an acute triangle located?

options.C: At the midpoint of the hypotenuse

questions.explanation: The circumcenter of an acute triangle is inside the triangle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Where is the circumcenter of a right triangle located?

options.C: At the midpoint of the hypotenuse

questions.explanation: The circumcenter of a right triangle is at the midpoint of the hypotenuse.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Where is the circumcenter of an obtuse triangle located?

options.C: At the midpoint of the hypotenuse

questions.explanation: The circumcenter of an obtuse triangle is outside the triangle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Where is the orthocenter of an acute triangle located?

options.C: At the midpoint of the hypotenuse

questions.explanation: The orthocenter of an acute triangle is inside the triangle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Where is the orthocenter of a right triangle located?

options.C: At the midpoint of the hypotenuse

questions.explanation: The orthocenter of a right triangle is at the right-angle vertex.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Where is the orthocenter of an obtuse triangle located?

options.C: At the midpoint of the hypotenuse

questions.explanation: The orthocenter of an obtuse triangle is outside the triangle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The circle inside a triangle tangent to all three sides is called the:
questions.explanation: The incircle of a triangle is the circle inside the triangle tangent to all three sides.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The circle passing through all three vertices of a triangle is called the:
questions.explanation: The circumcircle of a triangle is the circle passing through all three vertices.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Triangles having the same shape and the same size are called:
questions.explanation: Congruent triangles have the same shape and the same size; their corresponding sides and angles are equal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What does SSS congruence mean?

options.A: Side-Side-Side: three sides of one triangle equal the three corresponding sides of another

questions.explanation: SSS (Side-Side-Side) congruence: if the three sides of one triangle equal the three corresponding sides of another, the triangles are congruent.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What does SAS congruence mean?

options.A: Two corresponding sides and the included angle are equal
options.C: Two angles and the included side are equal
options.D: Hypotenuse and one side are equal

questions.explanation: SAS (Side-Angle-Side) congruence: two corresponding sides and the included angle are equal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What does ASA congruence mean?

options.A: Two corresponding angles and the included side are equal
options.C: Two sides and the included angle are equal
options.D: Hypotenuse and one side are equal

questions.explanation: ASA (Angle-Side-Angle) congruence: two corresponding angles and the included side are equal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What does AAS congruence mean?

options.A: Two corresponding angles and a corresponding non-included side are equal
options.C: Two sides and the included angle are equal
options.D: Hypotenuse and one side are equal

questions.explanation: AAS (Angle-Angle-Side) congruence: two corresponding angles and a corresponding non-included side are equal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What does RHS congruence mean?

options.A: In two right triangles, the hypotenuse and one corresponding side are equal
options.C: Two angles and the included side are equal
options.D: Two sides and the included angle are equal

questions.explanation: RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side) congruence: in two right triangles, the hypotenuse and one corresponding side are equal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Is AAA a triangle congruence test?

options.B: No, AAA establishes similarity, not necessarily congruence

questions.explanation: AAA is not a congruence test. AAA establishes similarity, not necessarily congruence.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Triangles having equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding sides are called:
questions.explanation: Similar triangles have equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding sides; they have the same shape but may differ in size.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What does AA similarity mean?

options.A: If two angles of one triangle equal two angles of another, the triangles are similar
options.B: If three sides are equal, triangles are similar
options.C: If two sides and included angle are equal, triangles are similar
options.D: If hypotenuse and one side are equal, triangles are similar

questions.explanation: AA similarity: if two angles of one triangle equal two angles of another, the triangles are similar.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: In similar triangles, all pairs of corresponding sides have:
questions.explanation: In similar triangles, all pairs of corresponding sides have the same ratio.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: How do the perimeters of similar triangles compare?

options.A: Their ratio equals the square of the ratio of corresponding side lengths
options.B: Their ratio equals the ratio of corresponding side lengths

questions.explanation: The ratio of perimeters of similar triangles equals the ratio of corresponding side lengths.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: How do the areas of similar triangles compare?

options.A: Their ratio equals the ratio of corresponding side lengths
options.B: Their ratio equals the square of the ratio of corresponding side lengths

questions.explanation: The ratio of areas of similar triangles equals the square of the ratio of corresponding side lengths.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If corresponding sides of similar triangles are in the ratio 2:3, what is their area ratio?
questions.explanation: The area ratio is the square of the side ratio: (2/3)² = 4/9, so 4:9.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales theorem) in a triangle?

options.A: A line drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides divides those two sides in the same ratio
options.B: The sum of two sides equals the third side
options.C: All angles of a triangle are equal

questions.explanation: The Basic Proportionality Theorem states that a line drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides divides those two sides in the same ratio.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the converse of the Basic Proportionality Theorem?

options.A: If a line divides two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, it is parallel to the third side
options.B: If a line is parallel to one side, it bisects the other two sides
options.C: If two triangles are similar, their sides are equal
options.D: If a line bisects an angle, it is parallel to the opposite side

questions.explanation: The converse states that if a line divides two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, it is parallel to the third side.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A polygon with four sides, four vertices and four interior angles is called a:
questions.explanation: A quadrilateral is a polygon with four sides, four vertices and four interior angles.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral?
questions.explanation: The sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral is 360°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the sum of the exterior angles of any convex polygon, including a quadrilateral?

options.D: It depends on the number of sides

questions.explanation: The sum of the exterior angles of any convex polygon, taking one exterior angle at each vertex in the same direction, is 360°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A quadrilateral in which both pairs of opposite sides are parallel is called a:
questions.explanation: A parallelogram is a quadrilateral in which both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a property of a parallelogram?

options.A: Opposite sides are parallel and equal

questions.explanation: The properties of a parallelogram are: opposite sides are parallel and equal; opposite angles are equal; adjacent angles are supplementary; and diagonals bisect each other. Diagonals being equal is a property of a rectangle, not a general parallelogram.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: In a parallelogram, adjacent angles are:
questions.explanation: In a parallelogram, adjacent angles are supplementary.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A parallelogram with four right angles is called a:
questions.explanation: A rectangle is a parallelogram with four right angles.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which property distinguishes a rectangle from a general parallelogram?

options.C: All angles are 90° and diagonals are equal

questions.explanation: A rectangle has all angles 90° and its diagonals are equal and bisect each other. A general parallelogram has neither of these properties.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A quadrilateral with four equal sides and four right angles is called a:
questions.explanation: A square is a quadrilateral with four equal sides and four right angles.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the diagonals of a square?

options.B: They are equal, perpendicular, bisect each other and bisect the vertex angles
options.D: They are equal but not perpendicular

questions.explanation: The diagonals of a square are equal, perpendicular, bisect each other and bisect the vertex angles.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A parallelogram with all four sides equal is called a:
questions.explanation: A rhombus is a parallelogram with all four sides equal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The diagonals of a rhombus:

options.B: Bisect each other at right angles and bisect opposite angles
options.C: Are always equal to the sides

questions.explanation: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles and bisect opposite angles.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a rhombus is FALSE?

options.D: Diagonals bisect each other at right angles

questions.explanation: A rhombus has equal sides, but its angles need not be 90°. Only a square (a special rhombus) has all angles 90°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: In Indian/British school terminology, a quadrilateral with one pair of opposite sides parallel is called a:
questions.explanation: A trapezium is a quadrilateral with one pair of opposite sides parallel. Some curricula use the term trapezoid differently.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A trapezium whose non-parallel sides are equal is called an:
questions.explanation: An isosceles trapezium is a trapezium whose non-parallel sides are equal; its base angles and diagonals are equal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: In an isosceles trapezium, which of the following is true?

options.A: Only the parallel sides are equal
options.B: Base angles and diagonals are equal

questions.explanation: In an isosceles trapezium, the base angles and diagonals are equal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A quadrilateral with two distinct pairs of adjacent equal sides is called a:
questions.explanation: A kite is a quadrilateral with two distinct pairs of adjacent equal sides.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following is a common property of a kite?
questions.explanation: In a kite, the diagonals are perpendicular; one diagonal bisects the other, and one pair of opposite angles is equal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A line segment joining two non-adjacent vertices of a polygon is called a:
questions.explanation: A diagonal of a polygon is a line segment joining two non-adjacent vertices.

questions.explanation: Distance = √[(4-1)² + (6-2)²] = √25 = 5 units.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following is a common examination error?

options.A: Confusing a line, line segment and ray
options.C: Applying the triangle angle sum correctly
options.D: Using perpendicular height in area formulas

questions.explanation: Do not confuse a line, line segment and ray; only a segment has two endpoints.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Complementary angles sum to ___ while supplementary angles sum to ___.
questions.explanation: Complementary angles sum to 90°; supplementary angles sum to 180°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Vertically opposite angles are equal; adjacent angles are not automatically equal
options.D: Linear pair angles are always equal

questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal; adjacent angles are not automatically equal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The triangle angle sum is ___ while the quadrilateral angle sum is ___.
questions.explanation: The triangle angle sum is 180°, while the quadrilateral angle sum is 360°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The exterior angle of a triangle equals:

options.B: The sum of the two remote interior angles
options.C: The difference of the two remote interior angles

questions.explanation: The exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: In area formulas, one should use:

options.B: Perpendicular height, not a slant side

questions.explanation: Use perpendicular height, not a slant side, in area formulas.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: In Pythagoras' theorem, c must be:

options.C: The hypotenuse, the side opposite the right angle

questions.explanation: In Pythagoras' theorem, c must be the hypotenuse, the side opposite the right angle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: A rectangle is necessarily a square
options.B: A square is both a rectangle and a rhombus

questions.explanation: A square is both a rectangle and a rhombus. A rectangle is not necessarily a square.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A rhombus has equal sides, but:

options.D: Its opposite sides must be unequal

questions.explanation: A rhombus has equal sides, but its angles need not be 90°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A diameter is:

options.B: The longest chord and equals twice the radius

questions.explanation: A diameter is the longest chord and equals twice the radius.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the:
questions.explanation: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: For a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are:
questions.explanation: For a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which units should be used for area?
questions.explanation: Use square units for area and linear units for perimeter or circumference.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which units should be used for perimeter or circumference?
questions.explanation: Use linear units for perimeter or circumference.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: In polygon formulas, n represents:
questions.explanation: In polygon formulas, n is the number of sides; check whether the question asks for interior sum, one interior angle or one exterior angle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: For similar figures, areas scale by:

options.B: The square of the side scale factor
options.C: The cube of the side scale factor

questions.explanation: For similar figures, areas scale by the square of the side scale factor.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: An angle of 35° is what type of angle?
questions.explanation: 35° is greater than 0° but less than 90°, so it is an acute angle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The complement of 28° is:
questions.explanation: The complement is 90° - 28° = 62°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The supplement of 115° is:
questions.explanation: The supplement is 180° - 115° = 65°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Vertically opposite angles are always:
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are always equal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Angles around a point add up to:
questions.explanation: Angles around a point add up to 360°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The sum of the interior angles of a triangle is:
questions.explanation: The sum of the interior angles of a triangle is 180°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The equal angles of an equilateral triangle are each:
questions.explanation: Each angle of an equilateral triangle is 60°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The longest side of a right-angled triangle is called the:
questions.explanation: The longest side of a right-angled triangle is called the hypotenuse.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 5 cm and 12 cm is:
questions.explanation: Hypotenuse = √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm is:
questions.explanation: Area = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 cm².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The sum of interior angles of a quadrilateral is:
questions.explanation: The sum of interior angles of a quadrilateral is 360°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are:
questions.explanation: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel and equal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The diagonals of a rectangle are:
questions.explanation: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The diagonals of a rhombus intersect at:

options.B: Right angles and bisect each other

questions.explanation: The diagonals of a rhombus intersect at right angles and bisect each other.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The area of a square of side 8 cm is:
questions.explanation: Area = side × side = 8 × 8 = 64 cm².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The diameter of a circle of radius 9 cm is:
questions.explanation: Diameter = 2 × radius = 2 × 9 = 18 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The longest chord of a circle is:
questions.explanation: The longest chord of a circle is the diameter.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the:
questions.explanation: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

questions.explanation: Number of diagonals = n(n-3)/2 = 6×3/2 = 9.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Each exterior angle of a regular octagon is:
questions.explanation: Each exterior angle = 360°/8 = 45°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The area ratio of similar triangles with side ratio 2:3 is:
questions.explanation: Area ratio = (2/3)² = 4/9, so 4:9.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a triangle centre?
questions.explanation: Midpoint is not a triangle centre. The triangle centres are centroid, incenter, circumcenter and orthocenter.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a congruence test?
questions.explanation: AAA establishes similarity, not congruence.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following is a property of a cyclic quadrilateral?
questions.explanation: In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a property of a square?
questions.explanation: The diagonals of a square are not parallel; they are perpendicular.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a property of a parallelogram?
questions.explanation: Diagonals being equal is a property of a rectangle, not a general parallelogram.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a property of a rhombus?

options.D: Diagonals bisect each other at right angles

questions.explanation: A rhombus has equal sides, but its angles need not be 90°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a circle theorem?

options.A: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference
options.B: Angles in the same segment are equal
options.C: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary
options.D: All chords of a circle are equal

questions.explanation: All chords of a circle are not equal; only chords equidistant from the centre are equal.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a polygon angle formula?
questions.explanation: The correct formula for the number of diagonals is n(n - 3) / 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a symmetry concept?
questions.explanation: Pythagorean symmetry is not a standard symmetry concept. Line symmetry and rotational symmetry (with its order) are the standard concepts.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a coordinate geometry formula?
questions.explanation: The slope formula is not covered in the supplied 8.3 Geometry notes. The notes cover distance and midpoint formulas only.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a circle measurement formula?
questions.explanation: Volume = πr³ is not a circle measurement formula (it is related to sphere volume, not covered in these notes). The notes cover circumference, area, arc length and sector area.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a formula from the consolidated formula sheet?
questions.explanation: The angle sum of a triangle is 180°, not 360°. The other three are correct formulas/properties.
